Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 106, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah Quraysh (Surah al-Ilaf)

It is Makki.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For the covenant of Quraysh﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, ﴿For the covenant of Quraysh﴾, that he said: My blessing upon Quraysh by their covenant of the caravan of winter and summer.

Al-Ilaf in the language (lughah) is the opposite of al-Ijash, and it is the counterpart of al-Ination. If someone asks: What is the meaning of the surah beginning with the lam? The answer has two aspects. The first is that its meaning is: Be amazed at the covenant of Quraysh and their abandoning of belief in Me, as if He is mentioning His blessing upon them and mentioning their ingratitude for His blessing by abandoning belief. The second aspect is that its meaning is: this is connected in meaning to the preceding surah, and it is as if He said: ﴿And He made them like eaten straw, for the covenant of Quraysh﴾, that is, so that what they had grown accustomed to of the caravans of winter and summer would remain for them.

Al-Qutabi mentioned concerning the meaning of the surah: the people had no crops or livestock except a little, and their livelihood was from trade, and they had two caravans: a caravan in summer to al-Sham, and a caravan in winter to Yemen. It was also said other than this. When they left Makkah, no one would confront them, and if a people met them, they would say: We are the people of Allah, so they would refrain from them and would not be opposed.

It is narrated that they used to say: We are from the Sanctuary of Allah, so the Arabs would say: These are the people of Allah, so they would refrain from them. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾. So Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in this surah and the preceding surah His favour upon them in repelling the People of the Elephant from them, so that what they had grown accustomed to of trade in the two caravans of winter and summer would remain for them.

As for Quraysh: they are the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah, so everyone who is a descendant of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah is Qurashi. They differed over the derivation of this name. Most of them said: they were named Quraysh for trade, as they were people of commerce, and al-qarsh means earning; it is said: so-and-so used to qarrash for his dependants and iqtarash, meaning he earned.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that Quraysh was named Quraysh after an animal in the sea called al-qirsh, which does not pass by anything lean or fat without eating it, and they recited concerning that:

(Quraysh is the one that dwells in the sea... and by it Quraysh was named Quraysh)

(It eats the lean and the fat and leaves not... in it for the one with two wings a feather)

(Thus in the lands Quraysh are... they devour the lands with a voracious devouring)

(And for them at the end of time there is a Prophet... who will increase killing among them and wounding)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 106, verses 3–4:

And His saying: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger﴾. He said this because they used to bring provisions from distant places, and it was He who made that easy for them and provided them with it by facilitating its means for them.

And His saying: ﴿and made them secure from fear﴾, meaning: from the fear of raids and killing, as we have said. It was also said: from the fear of leprosy (judhham). The more correct view is the first.

In some tafsir works: the first to bring the Quraysh together on the journeys of winter and summer was Hashim ibn 'Abd Manaf, and they would take from their merchandise, in the name of the poor, a specified portion; then, when they returned, they would give it to them, seeking nearness to God.

And the poet said about Hashim:

(ʿAmr al-ʿUlā hashsham al-tharīd li-qawmihi ... wa-rijāl Makkata musnatūna ʿijāf)
(Al-khālițīn faqīrahum bi-ghaniyyihim ... ḥattā yaṣīra faqīruhum ka-l-kāf)
